stories.h: Johnny Depp's 'Ebenezer' tops the global box office with $42m
stories.why: Weekend snapshot of what is playing worldwide
sum: Paramount's 'Ebenezer' opened at number one worldwide over 13-15 November, taking roughly $42m from 64 territories, split between about $23m internationally and $19m domestically. It is Johnny Depp's first chart-topper since 2018.

Sony's 'Ramayana: Rise of a Legend' held strongly in second place with $38.1m in its second weekend, a 34% drop, lifting its total to $147.5m. 'The Cat in the Hat' and 'Godzilla Minus Zero' rounded out the top four, while 'How to Rob a Bank' debuted with $10.3m.
pts: Ebenezer: about $42m opening across 64 markets
Ramayana: Rise of a Legend now at $147.5m
How to Rob a Bank opened at $10.3m

stories.h: 'Ebenezer' leads UK-Ireland chart as 'I Play Rocky' surges
stories.why: UK-side look at the same weekend
sum: Johnny Depp's 'Ebenezer' debuted at the top of the UK-Ireland chart with £4m from 634 sites, the biggest opening for any adaptation of A Christmas Carol and ahead of the 2009 version's £1.9m start.

The real surprise was 'I Play Rocky', which jumped from tenth to second after expanding from 148 to 624 locations, earning £1.1m for a £2.3m total. 'Ramayana: Rise of a Legend' dropped to third, and the top five together grossed £7.5m, up 25% on the previous weekend.
pts: Ebenezer opened with £4m, a Christmas Carol record
I Play Rocky climbed from 10th to 2nd
Top five up 25% week on week

stories.h: Bafta Scotland 2026: 'I Swear' leads film winners
stories.why: Awards-season signal for British and Scottish film
sum: Bafta Scotland announced its 2026 winners, with 'I Swear' named best feature film and taking three prizes in total, including best film actor for Robert Aramayo and best fiction director for Kirk Jones.

Lesley Manville won best film actress for 'Midwinter Break', and Maggie O'Farrell took the writing award for 'Hamnet'. On television, Robert Carlyle won for 'The Hack' and 'Outlander' received the outstanding contribution award.
pts: I Swear: best feature plus acting and directing wins
Lesley Manville wins for Midwinter Break
Maggie O'Farrell honoured for Hamnet script

stories.h: The Brit List 2026 names 13 unproduced UK screenplays
stories.why: Early look at future British film and TV
sum: The 19th Brit List, which highlights the best unproduced scripts by emerging UK writers, has been unveiled. Gemma Addy's wartime coming-of-age feature 'Dig For Victory' and Archie Thomson's crime series 'Petroc' lead with 25 recommendations each.

The bar for entry rose to 10 recommendations from seven last year, and six of the 13 projects still have no producer attached. Disney+ sponsors for the first time, and the chosen writers join a six-month development programme.
pts: 13 scripts selected; Dig For Victory and Petroc top the list
Six projects have no producers yet
Disney+ is headline sponsor for the first time

stories.h: Beyoncé hits 100 Grammy nominations; Kendrick only as a feature
stories.why: Both of your artists in one nominations list
sum: The 2027 Grammy nominations landed on November 16. Beyoncé becomes the first artist to reach 100 career nominations, thanks to her July 4 surprise song "Morning Dew (Donk)" being nominated in an R&B performance category.
Kendrick Lamar has no lead-artist nod this cycle. His only mention is as a guest on Baby Keem's "Good Flirts", up for Best Rap Performance. The ceremony airs February 7.
pts: Beyoncé: 100th career nomination via "Morning Dew (Donk)"
Kendrick Lamar: featured on Baby Keem's "Good Flirts" (Best Rap Performance)
Grammys air February 7 in Los Angeles

stories.h: Album of the Year nominees: Phoebe Bridgers, Rosalía, Swift and more
stories.why: Phoebe Bridgers in the big category
sum: The eight Album of the Year nominees are Phoebe Bridgers, Olivia Dean, Ella Langley, Bruno Mars, RAYE, Olivia Rodrigo, Rosalía and Taylor Swift.
Swift's nod is her eighth in the category, tying Frank Sinatra for the all-time record. Bridgers is the indie-leaning name on the list with Lost Weekend.
pts: Bridgers' Lost Weekend is nominated
Swift ties Sinatra with eight AOTY nods
Rosalía nominated for LUX (Complete Works)

stories.h: Geese and Angine de Poitrine among first-time Grammy nominees
stories.why: Indie and alt names breaking into the Grammys
sum: Best New Artist includes Geese, Angine de Poitrine, Slayyyter, Sienna Spiro, Remi Wolf and the Womack Sisters, all first-timers. Alex G earned his first Best Rock Song nod as part of the team behind Bridgers' "Lost Boys".
Other firsts include John Cale for "House" with Charli XCX, Yves Tumor for "Berghain" with Rosalía and Björk, and Denzel Curry in Best Metal Performance.
pts: Geese in Best New Artist
Alex G nominated for Best Rock Song
Yves Tumor and John Cale get first nods

stories.h: Hayley Williams curates Outbreak Festival 2027 in Manchester
stories.why: Alt-rock and indie heavy lineup
sum: Outbreak returns June 19 and 20, 2027 at Manchester's B.E.C. Arena, curated by Hayley Williams, who also headlines with her own show.

The bill leans emo and indie: Dinosaur Jr., Blood Orange, American Football, Julien Baker, Wednesday, Mannequin Pussy and Failure, with more to come. Presale opens November 18 and general sale November 19.
pts: June 19-20, 2027, Manchester
Dinosaur Jr., Wednesday, Julien Baker on the bill
Presale Nov 18, general sale Nov 19

stories.h: bdrmm return heavier with "Amuse Yourself"
stories.why: Shoegaze and alt-rock
sum: The Hull shoegaze band, now a trio after last year's Microtonic, share a heavy, industrial-tinged single.
Frontman Ryan Smith wrote it after an ADHD diagnosis and struggles with addiction, drawing on Ballard, Burroughs and writing about paranoia. UK and European dates run April 21 to May 22.
pts: Shoegaze with an industrial edge
Band is now a trio
Spring 2027 tour announced

stories.h: Hot Chip enlist Beth Ditto for "Me In Your Head"
stories.why: Indie dance with an alt-rock guest
sum: Hot Chip share a new single featuring Beth Ditto ahead of A Long Way From Kansas, their first studio album in five years.
The record is due January 8 on Domino.
pts: Feat. Beth Ditto
A Long Way From Kansas due Jan 8
First album in five years
stories.q: Hot Chip Me In Your Head Beth Ditto

stories.h: heavensouls' ten-minute "today i learned to fly again"
stories.why: Shoegaze-leaning, genre-blurring
sum: Houston-based producer Chidi Obialo, who records as heavensouls, released a ten-minute single built from stacked shoegaze guitars and distant field-recording textures.
Loud live drums arrive near the end and make it feel urgent. His EP cantu of the sower recently earned Best New Music from Pitchfork.
pts: Ambient shoegaze, ten minutes
Drums enter late for a big finish
Follows a Best New Music EP
stories.q: heavensouls today i learned to fly again

stories.h: Tyler, the Creator plays rarities at Camp Flog Gnaw
stories.why: Adjacent to your Kendrick taste in rap
sum: Tyler headlined the 12th Camp Flog Gnaw at Dodger Stadium, arriving in a prop plane and performing a 22-song set.
He revived Cherry Bomb and Bastard-era songs like "Seven" and "VCR", debuted new tracks, then told complaining fans he hated them.
pts: 22-track set with long-gap returns
Several live debuts
Plane stage entrance

stories.h: HOKA x MARNI Clifton MARNI lands in orange, white, black
stories.why: Quirky colour on a running shoe, easy to wear casually
sum: HOKA and MARNI are back for a second collab, this time rebuilding the Clifton 11 daily trainer with Marni's playful take on colour and texture. It comes in orange, white and black and costs £255.

Details include a plaid sockliner, metallic lace tips, reflective trim and a 3D silicone print, plus two extra pairs of laces for mixing it up. It hit MARNI stores and MARNI.com on 12 November, then HOKA and select retailers a day later.
pts: Orange, white and black colourways, £255
Plaid sockliner, metallic lace tips, extra laces
Out now via MARNI first, then HOKA

stories.h: ASICS x JUNTAE KIM GEL-KINETIC FR drops 20 Nov with detachable flowers
stories.why: Whimsical, niche sneaker with a customisable look
sum: Seoul designer JUNTAE KIM makes his first footwear collab with ASICS, a hybrid dress sneaker called the GEL-KINETIC FR. It comes in black, navy and red.

Gradients across the upper, toe and stripes mimic petals fading as they dry. Detachable floral hardware styled like withered petals and stamens clips on or off, so the shoe flips between dressy and streetwear. Leathers sit on ASICS runner tooling.
pts: Black, navy and red colourways
Removable floral hardware
On sale 20 November via ASICS and select retailers

stories.h: Adidas x Rick Owens revive the Springblade runner and boot
stories.why: Rock-edged, dark-leaning footwear
sum: Rick Owens and adidas are bringing back the Springblade for FW26 as a three-piece capsule: two low-top runners and a slouchy boot.

The runners come in inverted black and light brown, while the boot is Core Black with light brown accents. It releases 17 November through the adidas CONFIRMED app, both brands' sites and select retailers.
pts: Two runners plus one boot
Black and light brown palette
Release 17 November

stories.h: Tyler, the Creator and Converse chop down the Bronco Boot
stories.why: Colourful, casual and a little offbeat
sum: Converse and Tyler, the Creator's GOLF le FLEUR* line adds the Bronco Boot Low, a shortened everyday version of last year's rugged boot. Colourways are Cocoa Brown, New Wheat, Eden and Black.

It uses suede and leather uppers, a moulded rubber toe cap, lugged outsole, woven round laces and a le FLEUR* lace jewel. The same collection includes a Pro Leather and a Jogger in High Risk Red and Golden Haze. Available now.
pts: Four colourways incl. Eden green
Jogger in High Risk Red and Golden Haze
Out now at Converse and GOLF le FLEUR*

stories.h: Melissa x The Powerpuff Girls arrives with blind boxes and candy sandals
stories.why: Playful, colourful and nostalgic
sum: Melissa's first blind-box line features small scented figurines of Blossom, Bubbles and Buttercup, with a rare chase figure of villain H.I.M. They are made from Melissa's vegan PVC and smell like tutti-frutti.
Alongside are a candy-coloured Kitten Heel thong sandal for adults and kids' Mini Melissa Possession styles. It is available now on Melissa's site.
pts: Scented blind-box figurines with a chase piece
Candy-coloured kitten heel sandal
Available now

stories.h: VEJA x Marimekko put a pink-red paper-cut floral on the Salar
stories.why: Colourful print on an easy casual sneaker
sum: VEJA and Marimekko pair up on the adult Salar and kids' Small Canary, both wearing the Popkorni print, a floral motif cut from paper by Finnish artist Antti Kekki.

The pink and red pattern sits over recycled Alveomesh, with suede and traced leather panels on the Salar, bio-based midsoles and Amazonian rubber outsoles. The Small Canary adds red branding. Available now.
pts: Popkorni floral in pink and red
Recycled mesh, bio-based midsole
On sale now at VEJA

stories.h: Reebok and Tobe Nwigwe add a laceless Chukwu ATO and the ANO
stories.why: Pastel pops in a casual shoe
sum: Reebok and Tobe Nwigwe continue their partnership with two shoes: the Chukwu ATO, their first laceless sneaker, and the Chukwu ANO, the third and fourth signature silhouettes between them.
The ATO comes in Mint and Black, the ANO in Black/Gum and Salmon/Black. Both are available now at Reebok and select retailers.
pts: ATO in Mint and Black
ANO in Black/Gum and Salmon/Black
Out now

stories.h: Billie Eilish and BAPE release a first collab, camo and checks
stories.why: Baggy, casual, tomboy-friendly pieces
sum: Billie Eilish and BAPE have dropped their first collection together, built around oversized streetwear: a Camo Shark full-zip hoodie, varsity jacket, football jersey and matching basketball shorts.
It also has a checkered shirt, three graphic tees including a Baby Milo one, a rhinestone belt, camo cap, bandana and colourful socks. It is available now on BAPE's site and at select retailers.
pts: Camo hoodie, varsity jacket, jersey
Rhinestone belt, bandana, colourful socks
Out now

stories.h: Israeli strike hits Nasser Hospital in Khan Younis
stories.why: Gaza ceasefire violations and attacks on health care
sum: An Israeli airstrike hit the Nasser Medical Complex in Khan Younis shortly after midnight on 12 November, killing six people, among them a child, medical staff and patients, according to Mondoweiss. Gaza's Health Ministry says the surgical department was destroyed and more than 28 people were hurt; radiology and lab work were also disrupted.

Hospital director Ahmad al-Farra said two missiles struck, one failing to explode, and that no warning was given. He described it as the seventh time the hospital has been targeted during the war. The report also points to shortages of fuel and supplies across Gaza's health system.
pts: Six killed; Health Ministry reports over 28 injured, with figures varying by source
Director says no warning was issued and this is the hospital's seventh targeting
Strike adds pressure on a health system already short of fuel and supplies

stories.h: Strikes and a storm batter Gaza as truce talks stall
stories.why: Gaza humanitarian situation and ceasefire breakdown
sum: Local health sources say at least eight Palestinians were killed by Israeli attacks in Gaza on 10 November, including a father and his 13-year-old son, per the Wafa news agency. Gaza's Health Ministry says more than 1,600 people have been killed since the US-brokered truce took hold, and over 74,000 since October 2023.

The season's first strong storm flooded about 70,000 tents within 12 hours, the Government Media Office says. It claims Israel is blocking mobile homes and most tents. Negotiators remain split over Hamas disarmament and Israeli troop withdrawal, with Israel controlling roughly two-thirds of the territory.
pts: At least eight killed in one day, per local health sources
Storm flooded about 70,000 tents; Gaza officials say shelter entry is restricted
No deal yet on disarmament or Israeli withdrawal

stories.h: West Bank: 14-year-old killed in raid near Nablus
stories.why: West Bank violence and settler escalation
sum: Israeli forces shot dead 14-year-old Moataz Daghlas during a raid on Burqa near Nablus, the Palestinian Health Ministry said. Wafa reported two other teenagers were wounded, soldiers detained the boy's father, and an ambulance was obstructed. Israeli authorities are withholding his body.

The Israeli military said troops fired at people throwing stones at vehicles. The UN counts at least 1,143 Palestinians killed in the West Bank since October 2023, including 250 children and victims of settlers. ACLED says 2026 is on course to be the worst year on record for settler violence.
pts: Military says soldiers responded to stone-throwing; Palestinian sources dispute the circumstances
UN figure: 1,143 killed in the West Bank since October 2023
ACLED: record year for settler-related violence

stories.h: Civil society doubts Indonesia's COP31 forest pledges
stories.why: Land and environment conflicts, Papua
sum: At the COP31 talks in Antalya, Indonesia's delegation promised to protect forests, avoid clearing forest for farming and recognise 1.4 million hectares of customary forest. Civil society coalitions told Mongabay Indonesia the government is more eager to sell carbon credits, including through a platform listing 30 projects.

They point to a 2025 forestry decree that reclassified nearly 487,000 hectares in South Papua, record fire emissions, mangrove loss and continued captive coal plants. The groups want policy changes that match the rhetoric.
pts: Pledges include recognising 1.4 million hectares of customary forest
Coalitions cite the South Papua reclassification and fire emissions
Call to revoke policies that drive deforestation

stories.h: Activists protest RSPO over Indonesia's fires and palm oil
stories.why: Environmental conflict, corporate accountability
sum: On 3 November, groups including Walhi and TuK Indonesia demonstrated outside the RSPO annual conference in Tangerang, demanding accountability for forest and land fires. They argue certification lets palm oil firms greenwash, citing analyses that found burned land inside member concessions and hotspots overlapping orangutan habitat.

They want sanctions, supply-chain tracing and pressure on buyers, naming 15 global consumer brands. RSPO says only about 0.8 percent of burned area lay in member concessions, is investigating one complaint and has asked members for more transparency.
pts: Walhi and TuK Indonesia demand sanctions and traceability
RSPO disputes the scale, citing 0.8 percent of burned area
Fire analyses from different groups conflict

stories.h: Abdul El-Sayed becomes first Muslim elected to US Senate
stories.why: Muslim electoral win, Palestine politics in the US
sum: Progressive Democrat Abdul El-Sayed won Michigan's Senate seat and will be the first Muslim to serve in the chamber when Congress convenes in January. With 80 percent of votes counted he led Republican Mike Rogers 51.8 to 46.2, and AP called the race.

In his victory speech he criticised US funding for Israel's war on Gaza and said he beat AIPAC and other pro-Israel groups that spent heavily against him. He also answered attacks from Donald Trump and JD Vance over his name and religion.
pts: Won Michigan Senate seat; takes office in January
Said he defeated heavy pro-Israel group spending against him
Campaign faced attacks over his faith
